title: Мужские принципы и встреча со знакомой  (Male Principles and Running into an Acquaintance)

segments.t: Viktor Petrovich explains to an offended Elena that he has never wanted to depend on a woman and that women have always moved into his place instead. Back at the apartment, Kostya warns Max that the Chef will never forgive him, while Nastya hands a menu to a bride-to-be who turns out to be her old friend Katya.
Ну да, это уважительная причина.
Лена, я не хочу зависеть от кого-нибудь.
Тем более от женщин.
Всегда переезжали ко мне.
Я же говорил, починил.
Сейчас я открою.
Шеф, а вам удобно сейчас говорить?
Все равно он тебя не простит.
О, а помнишь, когда ты с Викой поругался?
Да не, не вариант.
Доброе утро.
Ваше меню.
Офигеть, это ты?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Ну да, это уважительная причина.

'Oh sure, that is a very valid reason.' Barinov favors a lively note in front of Elena, anchoring the Russian line on "uvazhitelnaya" ("valid, respectful") and "prichina" ("reason, cause") without extra filler.
Лена, я не хочу зависеть от кого-нибудь.
'Lena, I do not want to depend on anyone.' Max offers an unhurried footing on the spot, linking "khochu" ("want"), "zaviset" ("depends"), and "lena" ("Lena") in one brisk exchange.
Тем более от женщин.
'Especially not on a woman.' Elena presents a measured footing across the room, weaving "boleye" ("more") together with "zhenshchin" ("women") just the way native speakers do.
Всегда переезжали ко мне.

'Women have always moved in with me.' Barinov displays an unhurried course during the exchange, linking "vsegda" ("always"), "pereyezzhali" ("to move, to relocate"), and "ko" ("to") in one brisk exchange.
Я же говорил, починил.
'I told you I fixed it.' Max strikes an honest note across the room, joining "govoril" ("said, were saying") to "pochinil" ("fixed, repaired") so every word pulls its weight.
Сейчас я открою.
'Hold on, I will get the door.' Elena adopts a playful rhythm as they talk, combining "seychas" ("now") and "otkroyu" ("to open") so the key meaning lands right away.
Шеф, а вам удобно сейчас говорить?
'Chef, is this a convenient time for you to talk?' Max asks calmly as the talk turns, anchoring the Russian line on "udobno" ("comfortable") and "seychas" ("now") without extra filler.
Все равно он тебя не простит.
'He is not going to forgive you anyway.' Max maintains a warm view for Elena, putting "ravno" ("the same") alongside "prostit" ("will forgive") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
О, а помнишь, когда ты с Викой поругался?

'Oh, remember that time you had a huge fight with Vika?' Elena inquires bluntly for Barinov's benefit, linking "pomnish" ("do you remember"), "kogda" ("when"), and "porugalsya" ("to quarrel") in one brisk exchange.
Да не, не вариант.
'Nah, that is not an option.' Barinov keeps an emphatic style toward Max, building the phrase around "variant" ("option, variant") and "da" ("yes") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Доброе утро.
'Good morning to you.' Max favors an emphatic tone for Barinov, pairing "dobroye" ("good") with "utro" ("morning") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Ваше меню.
'Here is your menu.' Elena favors a sharp approach for Max, building the phrase around "menyu" ("menu") and "vashe" ("your") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Офигеть, это ты?
'No way, is that really you?' Barinov inquires calmly toward Elena here, building the phrase around "ofiget" ("to unbelievable") and "eto" ("this") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Ну да, это уважительная причина.
Лена, я не хочу зависеть от кого-нибудь.
Тем более от женщин.
Всегда переезжали ко мне.
Я же говорил, починил.
Сейчас я открою.
Шеф, а вам удобно сейчас говорить?
Все равно он тебя не простит.
О, а помнишь, когда ты с Викой поругался?
Да не, не вариант.
Доброе утро.
Ваше меню.
Офигеть, это ты?

That wraps up this scene as viktor Petrovich tells Elena he refuses to depend on a woman by living in her home, while at the restaurant Nastya is stunned to see her old acquaintance Katya. See you next time!
До свидания!
